From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>

Date: Tue, 02 Jun 2026 08:14:00 -0700
Subject: Quarterly review prep: customer health snapshot + renewal risk register

Team —

We have the Acme quarterly review next week and Procurement surfaced a potential early renewal request. I want us to align on customer health, the renewal risk register, and any items that need exec attention so we can present a concise ask. Please review the notes below and add any blocking items or missing context by EOD today.

Quick summary (initial):
- Renewal window: Aug 15 (primary renewal owner: Acme Procurement)
- Current utilization: ~56% of committed capacity (jobs spiky, nightly peaks)
- Support: 12 open tickets in last 30 days, 3 P2s (one still active)
- Financials: On-plan spend but forecast shows potential overage if usage spikes in July

What I need from each of you:
- Laura: updated renewal risk register + suggested mitigations for the exec slide
- Evelyn: latest customer health score and service incident timeline
- Aditya: a short list of runbook items and whether we can offer a short-term capacity burst without SLA changes

Attachments: please attach any scorecards or one-pagers. Ill collate into a single briefing for the exec sync at 10:30 PT on Thursday.

Jonas
Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 02 Jun 2026 10:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Quarterly review prep: customer health snapshot + renewal risk register

Jonas —

Thanks. I updated the renewal risk register and attached two artifacts (acme_renewal_scorecard.pdf, renewal_risk_register.xlsx). Highlights and proposed exec asks below.

Top risks (scored, 1-5):
- Usage variability (4): spikes during month-end runs are causing queue timeouts; suggests evaluating dedicated burst pool for July.
- Security evidence gap (3): Acme asked for additional audit logs retention examples; we can provide SOC2 excerpts but need a short one-pager for Procurement.
- Commercial cadence (3): Procurement is asking for an early pricing review; recommend a capped promotional credit rather than a discount.

Proposed exec asks (concise):
- Approve one-time 30% promotional credit up to $25k to address Procurement's early-renewal ask (owner: Sales).
- Approve short-term dedicated burst (up to 4 GPUs) for July (owner: Product Ops) — we can present cost/impact quickly.
- Sign off on a SOC2 evidence one-pager for Procurement (owner: Security/Compliance).

Flag: the churn probability (based on signals) is 18% if we dont address the usage and procurement asks.

Attachments: renewal_risk_register.xlsx (sheet: risks, mitigations, owners)

Laura 
Head of Renewals
Redwood Inference
From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 02 Jun 2026 11:28:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Quarterly review prep: customer health snapshot + renewal risk register

Laura / Jonas —

Quick ops update and feasibility notes:
- We can provision a short-term burst pool (4x A40-equivalent) for 3 weeks with ~48 hours lead time. Estimated incremental cost to Redwood: $18k; pass-through to customer or absorbed as credit per the proposed ask.
- Runbook: Ive attached a short runbook excerpt in the drive link (see related_links) describing the scale-up/scale-down steps and guardrails.
- Support tickets: the active P2 is tied to model load balancing; we expect a fix in 24-36 hours if we schedule a configuration tweak tonight.

Two asks for Product Ops / CS:
1) If exec approves burst, we need an approval window by EOD Wednesday to reserve capacity.
2) Please confirm whether we will frame the burst as a free courtesy (credit) vs billed line item in the renewal quote.

Happy to be on the call with Acme for technical Q&A.

—Aditya
Principal SRE, Redwood Inference

Adding the updated health metrics and a brief incident timeline:
- Customer health score (today): 68 / 100 (down from 76 last quarter).
- Contributing factors: increased error rates during nightly jobs (0.8% -> 2.3%), latency spikes (median 120ms -> 210ms for peak requests), and slower onboarding for a new internal Acme team.
- Incident timeline (last 30 days):
  - May 9: model timeout spike (resolved 6h)
  - May 22: job queue overflow (resolved 10h)
  - May 28: current P2 (investigating config)

Recommendation:
- Approve burst + temporary traffic shaping to stabilize latency before renewal conversations.
- Provide the SOC2 one-pager and a short remediation timeline to Procurement this week to reduce their risk perception.

Ill prepare a 1-slide health summary for the exec deck and attach the incident timeline.

Evelyn

- Approve one-time promotional credit up to $25k (Owner: Sales / Laura)
- Approve short-term burst pool (4 GPUs for 3 weeks) and sign-off on reservation by EOD Wed if accepted (Owner: Product Ops / Aditya)
- Sign and distribute SOC2 one-pager for Procurement (Owner: Security; contact: security@redwood.com)
- Exec slide: 1-slide health summary + incident timeline (Owner: Evelyn)

Action items (who does what by when):
- Laura: finalize renewal_risk_register.xlsx and provide the exact credit language for the exec slide (by Wed 12pm PT).
- Aditya: confirm cost breakdown and availability window (by Wed 3pm PT).
- Evelyn: attach health slide + incident timeline to the drive link (by Wed 5pm PT).
- Jonas: I will build the exec one-pager and coordinate the call with Acme for technical Q&A.
